validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION/SPEC confirmed independently of the sheet's own cited sources. The wiki page's only load-bearing citation for this segment is EIA's generic 'naturalgas/data.php' navigation page (cite_note-eia0421-4), which is not a usable ref (orchestrator note: it's a navigation page, not a ref for any value) -- so I went to the primary FERC docket instead of the harvested pool. Found: FERC Docket CP18-530-000, a NGA section 157.205/157.211 PRIOR NOTICE (not a full certificate case) filed by Florida Gas Transmission, LLC on July 19, 2018, 'requesting authorization to construct/modify, own, maintain and operate, certain natural gas mainline facilities and appurtenances in Santa Rosa County, Florida, and modify an existing delivery point, in Escambia County, Alabama for its South Alabama Project. FGT's South Alabama Project would provide up to 60,000 million British thermal units per day of firm transportation service to two shippers... FGT estimates the cost of the proposed project to be approximately $7,000,000' (Federal Register notice, govinfo.gov, an official government publication of the FERC filing). Independently, EIA's 'Natural Gas Pipeline Projects' workbook (a separately compiled statistical tabulation, not a copy of the FERC filing) carries a 'South Alabama Project' row: Pipeline Operator Name 'Florida Gas Trans Co', Docket CP18-530, Status 'Completed', Completed Date 2018-11-26, Year In Service 2018, Additional Capacity 60.0 MMcf/d, States AL/FL, Notes 'Additional deliverability to industrial (Ascend Performance Materials) and electric power (PowerSouth Energy Cooperative) consumers' -- this exact row is STILL present, unchanged, in EIA's current live workbook (EIA-NaturalGasPipelineProjectsAug2026.xlsx, 'Historical Projects (1996-2024)' tab), confirming it remains part of the operating system. A third, independent FERC document -- the Commission's own July 2018 'Energy Infrastructure Update' monthly bulletin -- states: 'Florida Gas requests authorization for its South Alabama Project, which includes replacing a compressor in Santa Rosa County, FL, and modifying a delivery point in Escambia County, AL to increase deliverability by 60 MMcf/d.' All three sources agree: capacity 60 MMcf/d (CONFIRMS Capacity=60.00 MMcf/d), completed/in-service 2018 (CONFIRMS StartYear1=2018), and the project scope is a compressor replacement + delivery-point modification with NO new pipeline mileage (CONFIRMS LengthKnown=0.00 mi, and explains why Diameter is correctly left blank -- no new pipe was laid). CLASSIFICATION: correctly an interstate FGT expansion/deliverability project, not a gathering or intrastate line. DUPLICATE check against the 37-row roster: P2738 is NOT the same project as P0164/other roster pipelines, and within the FGT family it is distinct from 'FGT Western Division Project' (CP17-23, MS->AL, +69 MMcf/d, completed 2018-10-25 -- a different docket, different capacity, one month earlier) and from the later 'Southeast Alabama Project' (~2024-2025) and 'South Central Alabama Project' (2025-2026, CP26-26, +170,000 MMBtu/d) -- three separate, sequential FGT Alabama-panhandle expansions with distinct dockets/capacities/years; P2738=CP18-530 is the 2018 one. Existing value checks: Status='operating' CONFIRMED (EIA Completed + still live in the 2026 workbook + FGT's own current system-map page, fgttransfer.energytransfer.com/ipost/FGT/maps/system-map, resolves 200 and names Florida Gas Transmission Pipeline). Fuel='Gas' CONFIRMED (both FERC documents describe 'natural gas mainline facilities'). Owner1='Florida Gas Transmission Co LLC' 100% CONFIRMED as the correct operating/filing entity (both FERC docs name 'Florida Gas Transmission, LLC' as applicant). Citation-pool accounting: of the 9 citations harvested from the shared FGT wiki page, I opened/tested 3 (fgttransfer.energytransfer.com system-map: live, useful; kindermorgan.com/pages/business/gas_pipelines/east/FGT: dead, 404; the abarrelfull.wikidot.com bit.ly link: read for lead only, per standing rule 5 never citable) and did not open the remaining 6 (eia.gov/maps/layer_info-m.php -- generic state-map layer legend, not project-specific; eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php -- the navigation page already ruled out; fractracker.org's 2020 national map; oilandgaswatch.org/pipeline/6491 -- EIP's tracker, likely FGT-system-level, not opened given the three primary sources already in hand; the PGJ 2018 Planned-Projects PDF; texasenergyreport.com's 2018 East-West Pipeline Expansion article, which is about FGT's Texas/Louisiana CP17-8 project, not South Alabama). All three refs used were found independently via the Gulf Coast source ladder (FERC + EIA), not from the harvested pool.

validity.researcher_notes: The sheet's Location [ref] unit currently carries StartState/Province='Mississippi', EndState/Province='Alabama'. All three independently-checked primary sources place the project's actual physical facilities in FLORIDA and ALABAMA, with no Mississippi involvement whatsoever: (1) the FERC Federal Register notice (govinfo.gov, CP18-530) states the facilities are 'certain natural gas mainline facilities and appurtenances in Santa Rosa County, Florida, and modify an existing delivery point, in Escambia County, Alabama'; (2) FERC's own July 2018 Energy Infrastructure Update states the project 'includes replacing a compressor in Santa Rosa County, FL, and modifying a delivery point in Escambia County, AL'; (3) EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook lists State(s)='AL,FL' with Beg_State='AL', End_State='FL' for this exact row (docket CP18-530, capacity 60.0, completed 2018-11-26). Three sources, two of them FERC's own documents describing the physical facility locations directly (not a copy of one another -- one is an individual docket notice, the other a monthly system-wide infrastructure bulletin), agree the states involved are Florida and Alabama. Mississippi does not appear in any source for this specific project (it likely bled in from a neighboring FGT row -- the CP17-23 'Western Division Project', completed one month earlier in Oct 2018, IS Mississippi->Alabama, +69 MMcf/d -- a plausible source of the mix-up, though I did not chase that further since it's out of this row's scope).
